# Results reported in the manuscript

<!-- Generated by scripts/render_reported_results.py from paper/reported_results.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**CROSS-MORSE: Cross-Spectral Control of Message Passing in Frozen Graph Neural Networks** — Abdolvahab Khalili Sadaghiani, Jose Nunez-Yanez (Linköping University, Linköping, Sweden). Scientific Reports manuscript.

These values are transcribed from the submitted manuscript PDFs (transcription date 2026-10-24) for comparison only. They include our reported measurements, derived quantities and analytical sensitivity calculations; [sources.json](sources.json) records their PDF identities, pages and evidence types. They are not new benchmark measurements from the bundled software-validation runs. See the [paper-results overview](../docs/PAPER_RESULTS.md) for interpretation and [results/replay guide](../docs/RESULTS.md) for comparison with a completed run. Units: losses in nats (CE or mean multilabel BCE); official metrics in percentage points except where a table states native AP; costs in units of one nominal full-depth execution; GPU-hours on one NVIDIA GH200 96 GB. Sign convention: paired loss effects q_D minus q_C; negative favours the deployed rule.

**Admission scope:** all reported admission decisions are descriptive. The three multi-graph benchmarks reused validation for confirmation and admission; their numerical bounds do not instantiate Theorem 2. The single-graph benchmarks use dependent cores or official splits. Main Table 1, p11; Supplementary Note S26, p31.

`paper/reported_results.json` also carries Supplementary Tables S6c (sensing-cost identity), S15b (per-rerun resource ledger), S16/S16b (factorials), S21 (action-gap audit), S22 (trajectory-tube audit), S23b (nominal execution time and amortization), S26b (ensemble law and break-even), S30 (oracle dispersion), S34 (budget-aware rule), S37 (input-fallback counts), S44 (per-input cost model), S45 (inserted-site attribution) and S47 (decision boundary and power), and the abstract's quantitative claims. `scripts/check_paper_constants.py` verifies the arithmetic that links these tables.
